Permit API: 083-46720
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2026
Comments: I conducted a follow up inspection of this conventional well that had a release occur in November of 2025, when a steel gathering line had ruptured resulting in crude oil contaminating ditches and soil. Initially the remediation of the site was progressing. There had been no signs of product at the under flow dams, there was no viable oil in the ditches. In preperation of obtaining confirmatory soil samples to evaluate if the remediation was sufficient, it was discovered another leak had developed on a different section of the same line. This operator indicated they will replace all of the steel line for this well with plastic/poly line. This release was caught early and as of now, appears to be less than 1 bbl of lost product and has impacted a minimal amount of soil.Bull Run employees had a roll off dumpster en-route to remove the impacted soil. The ruptured line was sucked out with a vac truck and will be removed while running new poly line. Further inspections will be conducted to document ongoing remedation efforts, as well as confirmatory sampling to show that the remediation is sufficient.

SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/08/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 987904
Permit API: 015-23753
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Terry Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/08/2023
Comments: On 3/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Incident - Response to Accident or Event inspection at the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 32 degrees and lightly snowing when I arrived on location. On 3/6/2023 Chesapeake personnel identified a water puddle on the unprotected pad surface with elevated conductance on the southwest corner of the pad in the location where chemical ASTs and a freshwater AST were stationed during recent frac operations. No release was reported in this area during the frac or drilling operations. It is expected that an unknown quantity of produced water or brine may have been released during fracking operations. They began excavating the area and had removed 20 truckloads when they contacted the department on 3/7/2023 to report the release. They continued removing material and were still excavating during this inspection. The excavated material was being hauled to the Chesapeake Stoorza well site for temporary storage prior to disposal.I met Creston Envirionmental's Andrew Steffe, who was field testing water and soil from and around the excavation. Andrew reported that he had gotten readings as high as 50 mS conductance from a water puddle that was in the area being excavated. Readings from the soils ranged from 0.1 mS conductance to 6.0 mS conductance. We measured the current extent of the excavation at 162' x 50'. It was approximately 3' deep. A water puddle in the bottom of west end of the excavated area field tested at 15.95 mS conductance. I field tested water in two test pits that were near the north side of the excavated area; water in the east pit was 6.13 mS conductance and the west pit was >20.0 mS conductance. The upper limit of the Oakton PCTS-50 is 20.0 mS conductance. Andrew said that the excavation would continue until he got readings that were under 1.0 mS conductance.I field tested water on the northeast corner of the pad with results at 1.3 mS, 0.5 mS, and 0.5 mS. Drilling mats were being pressure washed on the northwest corner of the pad, the washing being conducted over secondary containment. Water on the east side of the drilling mat wash station field tested at 1.4 mS conductance and on the west side field tested at 0.6 mS conductance. Water in the wash station secondary containment field tested at 1.8 mS conductance.There are five wells on site. Crews were in the process of putting the five wells into production. API/well permit numbers are posted at the entrance to the site. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank were not connected to the wellheads yet.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization was witnessed in some areas. PCSM is addressed on site by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. Temporary compost filter socks remain in place below the infiltration areasThis spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 56[a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b).The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c)I left the site at 1145 hrs.

Violation ID: 8170405
Permit API: 083-53759
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Foster Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/03/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to reported concerns at the tank battery located near this well. This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. There are no apparent surface issues on the location location or the spur road leading to it.A tank battery located along FR 370 approximately 250 feet northwest of this well consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks (11883 and 11884) within an earthen containment. There is evidence of repeated discharges of production water inside of the containment from each tank. Soil specific conductance (SPC) readings upwards of 15,000 uS/cm were detected at/downslope of the drains located on the back side of each tank. Elevated SPC is prevalent across the ground inside of the containment downslope of the tanks. Accumulated fluid pooled along the western wall of the containment has an SPC over 20,000 uS/cm. There was no active discharge at time of inspection.The fluids released inside of the containment have seeped through the northern corner of the earthen containment wall (or there is a buried drain) at 41.99216N / 78.76119 W. There is an approximate 25' x 3' area of stained soil with elevated SPC (upwards of 818 uS/cm vs 40 uS/cm of nearby uncontaminated soil) present outside of the containment's northern corner. The end of the apparent contaminated soil is located approximately 75 feet from Yeager Brook.Upon discovering the source, amount and extent of the releases at this tank battery, appropriate remediation options will be explored and documented in upcoming inspections. The inability for the tank battery containment to contain fluid inside of it will also nee to be addressed for compliance to be achieved.

Comments: I spoke with Brendon Logan (Chief) on site. He explained the compressor unit caught fire on January 16, 2021. Containment structures are intact; I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies today. There is no standing liquid on site today; it's all frozen (snow, ice). Air temp 22F JLP

Sample 0983-343 was collected from the rock-lined channel (photo #8). properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: XTO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/09/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 994371
Permit API: 035-21217
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Chapman Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/09/2023
Comments: On May 9, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline followed up on a reported spill of production fluid from a tanker truck at the XTO Energy PA Tract Pad A. The spill occurred on 9 different areas of Dry Run Rd. and the short access road to Well Pad A. The volume of the spill is unknown. DEP spoke with Jason Canose with XTO on the phone and he said he would notify DEP when the tanker truck off loads. XTO would have a better estimate of a volume after this occurs. The spills along Dry Run Rd. occurred early on May 9, 2023. The cause of the spill from the tanker truck is suspected to be an open scrubber valve on the tanker truck. XTO was still investigating the cause of the spill during the DEP follow up to the incident. The size of the spills along the short access road and Dry Run Rd. varied in size from approximately 140 ft. x 8 ft. to 15 ft. x 10 in. DEP and XTO delineated and marked the 9 different spill areas for XTO contractors to begin excavating the impacted soil. DEP screened the 9 different spill areas with a soil conductivity meter and all the spill areas had sections of the individual areas where the conductivity was over range of the meter. The upper limit of DEP's soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. The 9 spill areas were mostly contained to the road surface. The spills at mile 5.4 extended about 3 ft. off the road edge and at mile 9 extended about 2 ft. off the road edge. No wetlands or streams appeared to be impacted by the spills. XTO contractors had begun excavating multiple spill sites on Dry Run Rd. as DEP left the site. XTO plans to remediate the spill sites according to the Act 2 remediation standards.The spilling of production fluid outside of containment and onto the ground is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/25/2023 to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Twp, Bradford county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/25/2023
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 992501
Permit API: 015-23733
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/25/2023 at 0820 hours. The weather was 38 degrees with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted to summarize recent remedial activities since the last follow-up inspection on 4/10/2023 regarding a release from 4/6/2023. Blackhill has now had the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment structure removed from the impacted area. All material in this area that Blackhill discovered to have elevated electrical conductivity (EC) has been excavated (photos #1 and 2) and placed within lined waste containers or on secondary containment and covered (photo #3). I field measured water collected in the accessible portions of the excavated area shown in photos #1 and 2 and received readings of ~1.7mS/cm. Blackhill continues to have water that collects in these areas pumped out. The produced water tanks have been moved to a new location along the northern edge of the pad with a new secondary containment structure (photo #7). The yellow bin that holds the offload valve has now been placed further back so the entire bin is within secondary containment. Blackhill reported that elevated EC water was discovered along the buried produced water flowline. Portions of the pad material where the flowline was buried have now been excavated to a point where it can be done safely. The buried produced water flowline closest to the processing equipment has been "pot-holed" and elevated EC readings of ~2.7mS/cm were reported. Blackhill is in the process of devising a plan to continue excavation along the buried flowline safely.The entire southeastern stormwater basin (photo #4) has been excavated and Blackhill reported that field readings within the basin were now below 1.0mS/cm. A portion of the southern stormwater conveyance channel has been lined with plastic (photo #6) and a large sump was constructed just before the stormwater basin (photo #5). Blackhill reported that water collecting in the lined sump has been field measured below 1.0mS/cm. Blackhill is currently having stormwater collected from the excavated areas and secondary containments onsite following numerous rain events over the past few days.All violations associated with the release from 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time against API #015-23733. I departed the site at 1000 hours.

Comments: On 06/04/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) received a spill notification (CTS 389602) for Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) Kerrick Unit Well Pad in Asylum Township, Bradford County. It was discovered that stormwater mixed with produced water either overtopped the containment or there is a hole in the containment. It was estimated ~ 20 gallons were released. The stain is ~ 40' x 44' x 50' off containment. On 06/05/2025 the DEP conducted an incident inspection at the Kerrick Unit Well Pad. Expand representative Mike Deming accompanied me during the inspection. Mike stated that water in the area of the discovered release was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 7-8 mS/cm. The soil was also field measured for EC ~ 4 mS/cm. There was no pooled water on the pad at the time of the inspection. Mike stated on 06/04/2025 some material was recovered and placed in a lined dumpster onsite (photo #3-5). Approximately six inches of material was scraped. Remediation will resume once the produced fluid tank is removed. For further details reference Inspection Record No. 3990710.On 06/24/2025 the DEP conducted a Follow-Up Inspection at the Kerrick Well Pad. The weather was 89 degrees and sunny. I arrived at 1140 hours. The site appears stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There was an infiltration berm onsite. Pooled water in the area of the release was field measured for EC at ~1760 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank equipped with an internal secondary containment. The second produced fluid tank has been removed. There were five gas processing units (GPUs) onsite. There were five wells capable of producing onsite. They were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. The DEP recommends:1. Addressing the elevated pooled water onsite (photo #6 and 7). The following violations remain open against API #015-23861:35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)I departed at 1240 hours.

Comments: On 7/17/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection was conducted in response to notification from Seneca of the installation of a concrete catch basin and corrugated pipe on the north side of the pad to capture surface waters on the pad. It was 70 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. I was unaccompanied during the inspection. When I arrived on site, I observed a trench that had recently been dug along the north side of the pad, the trench leading to a 4' x 2' x 2' deep cement catch basin as seen in pictures 12, 13, and 14. Comments: On July 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4209208, where violations were continued for broken and corroded piping causing a release, as well as the issuance of new violations for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.Accompanying on today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4209208, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it, however the well tag does not appear to updated and the phone number listed on the tag is not in service. Violations are being continued at this time for having inaccurate information on the well tag/posting. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank ((3.80 mS and Over Range (>12mS)) and adjacent to the broken corroded pipe (0.329 mS). These conductivity readings were compared to a background soil conductivity reading of 0.181 mS collected upslope and away from the release area. The soil conductivity readings in the release area are elevated compared to background subjugating that the release from the back of the production tank on the right has yet to be remediated. Violations are being continued at this time for the release from the production tank.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment. Violations are being continued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. The Department is again requesting the Operator provide the Department with a Notice of Violation Operator response within 14 days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping, inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site is to remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: On July 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4209208, where violations were continued for broken and corroded piping causing a release, as well as the issuance of new violations for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.Accompanying on today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4209208, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it, however the well tag does not appear to updated and the phone number listed on the tag is not in service. Violations are being continued at this time for having inaccurate information on the well tag/posting. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank ((3.80 mS and Over Range (>12mS)) and adjacent to the broken corroded pipe (0.329 mS). These conductivity readings were compared to a background soil conductivity reading of 0.181 mS collected upslope and away from the release area. The soil conductivity readings in the release area are elevated compared to background subjugating that the release from the back of the production tank on the right has yet to be remediated. Violations are being continued at this time for the release from the production tank.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment. Violations are being continued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. The Department is again requesting the Operator provide the Department with a Notice of Violation Operator response within 14 days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping, inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site is to remain outstanding at this time.

The access road leading to the other wells had not appeared to have had maintenance (Photos 18, 19).Due to the observation of elevated conductivity readings within the tank battery remaining despite current remediation measures, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being issued.

Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone call made by Dan McCamey, of Minard Run Oil Company (MROC) on December 22, 2025. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred at Warrant 5107 Well #25P (API# 053-26767). A failure in the buried steel pipeline leading to this well resulted in leaking crude oil rising to the surface. A well tender spotted the crude oil earlier today and notified MROC immediately. A work crew arrived soon thereafter to repair the line, install containment, and begin remediating the released crude oil. Upon my arrival to the site, the pipeline had been repaired which stopped the release. The released crude oil had migrated down the road ditch for approximately 20 feet, across the road through a culvert, flowing downhill into a spring, ultimately entering Guiton Run (HQ-CWF) at (41.513992, -79.18582) after traveling approximately 50 yards. Pockets of weathered crude oil and emulsion were evident downstream for approximately 475 yards ending at (41.512156, -79.189991). The amount of crude oil released as a result of this incident was unknown due to the lack of accumulated product at the site. At this time, it is estimated that less than one barrel of product was released. A siphon dam was installed in the road ditch, beyond the direction of flow where the crude oil was initially spotted. A second siphon dam was installed and lined beyond the road culvert. Booms and diapers were already placed on the surface and at the point of entry in Guiton Run. Booms and diapers should be regularly monitored and replaced as necessary until the site is deemed remediated. Additional booms and diapers should be placed in Guiton Run to absorb and capture any released crude oil within the stream. The stream should be continuously monitored until there is no longer any evidence of crude oil. Follow up inspections will routinely be conducted to monitor remediation of this release. Confirmatory field screening and/or sampling will need to be conducted to verfiy that the cleanup is deemed complete prior to any seeding/mulching. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The conventional well was equipped for production with a pump jack. The well name, API number, and operator information were displayed on a sign attached to the pump jack.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-06-03 to Catalyst Energy Inc in Hamilton Twp, McKean county. SWMA 302(B)1 - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person failed to use methods or facilities necessary to control leachate, runoff, discharges and emissions from residual waste in accordance with DEP regulations.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Catalyst Energy Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-03
Violation Code: SWMA 302(B)1 - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person failed to use methods or facilities necessary to control leachate, runoff, discharges and emissions from residual waste in accordance with DEP regulations.
Violation ID: 886009
Permit API: 083-55763
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-03
Comments: This well is a producing combination well with an electric powered motor attached. The well was being operated at the time of this inspection. The stuffing box gasket failed, and at the time of visit, the well was pumping oil and brine out to the ground. The fluid plus runoff from recent rains allowed the oil to flow down the road approximately 150 feet, entering a puddle near a culvert that carried an UNT Chappel Fork. The operator was contacted to get cleanup efforts underway. The well was shut off and pads were placed down to collect as much oil from the track as possible. No oil was apparent in the UNT. Rain stopped and there was a decrease in the flow of oil down the track. The pumper for this lease showed up and was able to leave and get a vacuum truck to come collect the water/oil in the puddle. Marking tape was placed so that public vehicles would not drive through the oil. It is estimated that 15-20 gallons of fluid, including 3-5 gallons of oil were released from the well due to the stuffing box failure. Most pooled in a low spot next to the wellhead. Some ran down the access road, again pooling in a puddle of water that was previously mentioned. The brine mostly stayed in place in the soil or vegetation. A puddle within 10 feet of the wellhead showed over 20 mS/cm conductivity, while checking further toward the extent of the spill showed much lower numbers. The final puddle registered under 0.1 mS/cm. The operator had the vac truck on the way and after later discussions, it was decided that they would need to excavate the area around the wellhead to remove impacted soil. Further follow up will be done on this site as possible.

Comments: On January 5 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Ziolkowoski Well Site (NOT approved on 11/6/2023) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/4/2026 (CTS 394386). Present during the inspection was operator representative Nate Smiell.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel. The Department was unable to assess site stabilization due to snow coverage.At the time of inspection, there are 14 total wells on the well pad. According to Mr. Smiell, 8 of the wells (2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, 6H, 7H, 8H, and 9H) are completed/active wells. These wells were surrounded by protective barriers and appeared equipped for productions with well tags present. Mr. Smeill stated that stimulation for the other 6 wells (1H,10H,11H,12H,13H, and 14H) has been completed and they are currently in the process of drill outs for these wells.Upon inspection, all necessary drilling equipment appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No fluid leaks or spills were identified around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Smiell guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Smiell the release occurred on 1/4/2026. He stated the release was caused by 2 loose flange bolts on a 2-inch oil dump line located at the front of the #5 GPU. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of a produced water and condensate mixture released to the graveled well pad.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 4 foot radius around the #5 GPU. A background conductivity reading of 0.08mS was obtained. Conductivity readings of 2.76mS, 10.36mS, 2.14mS, and several readings of OR (Over Detectable Range, >20MS) were obtained in the area of the release. During the inspection, the Department observed active remediation of the spill occurring. Mr. Smiell stated that an air excavation/vacuum truck was being used to break up the ground and vacuum the contaminated material into waste containers. He stated that additional excavation by heavy machinery will occur as needed when the GPU is removed from its location as they plan to replace it upon competition of the active drill outs.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Comments: On January 5 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Ziolkowoski Well Site (NOT approved on 11/6/2023) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/4/2026 (CTS 394386). Present during the inspection was operator representative Nate Smiell.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel. The Department was unable to assess site stabilization due to snow coverage.At the time of inspection, there are 14 total wells on the well pad. According to Mr. Smiell, 8 of the wells (2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, 6H, 7H, 8H, and 9H) are completed/active wells. These wells were surrounded by protective barriers and appeared equipped for productions with well tags present. Mr. Smeill stated that stimulation for the other 6 wells (1H,10H,11H,12H,13H, and 14H) has been completed and they are currently in the process of drill outs for these wells.Upon inspection, all necessary drilling equipment appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No fluid leaks or spills were identified around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Smiell guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Smiell the release occurred on 1/4/2026. He stated the release was caused by 2 loose flange bolts on a 2-inch oil dump line located at the front of the #5 GPU. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of a produced water and condensate mixture released to the graveled well pad.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 4 foot radius around the #5 GPU. A background conductivity reading of 0.08mS was obtained. Conductivity readings of 2.76mS, 10.36mS, 2.14mS, and several readings of OR (Over Detectable Range, >20MS) were obtained in the area of the release. During the inspection, the Department observed active remediation of the spill occurring. Mr. Smiell stated that an air excavation/vacuum truck was being used to break up the ground and vacuum the contaminated material into waste containers. He stated that additional excavation by heavy machinery will occur as needed when the GPU is removed from its location as they plan to replace it upon competition of the active drill outs.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Violation ID: 8262516

Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/22/2026
Comments: This routine inspection was conducted in order to assess overall site conditions. Nine wells are staged for production on the well pad. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. Two dehydrators are also present within secondary containment. The dehydrators and containment appear to be in good condition. There are 3 batteries of frac tanks on the well pad, each with 10 tanks in each. The secondary containments for the tanks appear to be in good condition. I observed puddles on the pad surface in the offloading area of the southern frac tank battery. These puddles had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 9.32 mS/cm to 13.67 mS/cm. The puddles covered an area of the well pad approximately 20 ft by 5 ft. Puddles on other parts of the pad an EC readings of around 1500 uS/cm. A puddle on the access road present between the Bieber Sisters Well Pad and the entrance to the access road had an EC reading of 2.70 mS/cm. I took sample 0718-267 at 1340 from the puddles in the south frac tank battery offloading area. The sample was sent to the state laboratory to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Al, Sr, and Br on the same day.In a phone call with Rick Hall of EQT on 1/23/26 at 1051, Rick stated that the south battery of 10 frac tanks is being used for additional storage of produced fluid from the 9 nine producing wells on the pad, in addition to the 6 permanent production tanks present on the well pad. He said that the wells on the pad produce enough water that these frac tanks must be used for additional storage. He said that 10 to 12 water trucks visit the site to empty the tanks per day. He stated that he thought it was a strong possibility that the elevated conductivity is due to trucks tracking road salt onto the well pad since the paved portion of the access road, between the Bieber Sisters Pad and the Mallory A, has been heavily salted recently. A CSL 402(b) violation is noted. Additional violations may be assessed following receipt of the analytical results for sample 0718-267.

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8262516
Permit API: 081-21946
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/22/2026
Comments: This routine inspection was conducted in order to assess overall site conditions. Nine wells are staged for production on the well pad. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. Two dehydrators are also present within secondary containment. The dehydrators and containment appear to be in good condition. There are 3 batteries of frac tanks on the well pad, each with 10 tanks in each. The secondary containments for the tanks appear to be in good condition. I observed puddles on the pad surface in the offloading area of the southern frac tank battery. These puddles had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 9.32 mS/cm to 13.67 mS/cm. The puddles covered an area of the well pad approximately 20 ft by 5 ft. Puddles on other parts of the pad an EC readings of around 1500 uS/cm. A puddle on the access road present between the Bieber Sisters Well Pad and the entrance to the access road had an EC reading of 2.70 mS/cm. I took sample 0718-267 at 1340 from the puddles in the south frac tank battery offloading area. The sample was sent to the state laboratory to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Al, Sr, and Br on the same day.In a phone call with Rick Hall of EQT on 1/23/26 at 1051, Rick stated that the south battery of 10 frac tanks is being used for additional storage of produced fluid from the 9 nine producing wells on the pad, in addition to the 6 permanent production tanks present on the well pad. He said that the wells on the pad produce enough water that these frac tanks must be used for additional storage. He said that 10 to 12 water trucks visit the site to empty the tanks per day. He stated that he thought it was a strong possibility that the elevated conductivity is due to trucks tracking road salt onto the well pad since the paved portion of the access road, between the Bieber Sisters Pad and the Mallory A, has been heavily salted recently. A CSL 402(b) violation is noted. Additional violations may be assessed following receipt of the analytical results for sample 0718-267.
